installStep.name: What is in the core install

plugin.name: CEF and its box tokens
plugin.description:
The DLL, CostumeFW.esp and CostumeFW_BoxPool1.esp.
Both plugins are light (ESL) and take no load-order slot.
CostumeFW_BoxPool1.esp is new in 1.6.4 and is not optional. It carries three more box tokens for each biped slot, which is what lets one slot hold more than one box. It also carries the invisible physics carrier meshes those tokens need, which is most of the file count in this install.
Do not remove it once you have made a box on one of its tokens. That box goes dormant without it - it is not deleted, and it comes back when you put the plugin back, but until then it cannot be worn or edited.

plugin.name: Overwriting the CEF you already have (1.6.4 or older)
plugin.description:
Let your mod manager REPLACE it. Replace is the right answer for a CEF update: it clears the old mod out, puts this one in its place, and keeps its position in your mod order.
Do not pick Merge, and do not install this alongside the old one under a second name. CEF builds physics carrier meshes into its own mod folder and keeps a hash file beside each one. If those hash files survive while this archive's empty placeholder meshes land on top of the built ones, CEF finds a matching hash, skips the rebuild, and those boxes come back with no physics and nothing said about it. Replace clears both together, so the next launch rebuilds them.
Your boxes, presets and settings are not in the mod folder. They live in SKSE\Plugins\CEF_settings.json and in your save, and replacing the mod does not touch them.
If you are coming from 1.6.2 or earlier, there is one thing worth doing first. Up to 1.6.2 a costume's stats were handed to you through a spell built while the game was running. That spell does not exist on the next launch, but the bonus it applied is written into your save with nothing left to take it back off. 1.6.3 changed the mechanism so it cannot happen again, and it cannot clean up what is already stuck.
The clean fix is to go back to the version you have now, take every box token off, save, and then install this. If you have already updated, CEF adds up what it thinks the old mechanism was applying and shows it when the save loads; "cef abilities legacy" prints it again. To clear one by hand, read it with "player.getavinfo health" - or whichever value is wrong - and take it off with "player.modav health -N", using the number next to Perm. Subtract only what you can account for, because other mods' bonuses land in the same number.

plugin.name: Remove the old NPC add-on and VR patch first
plugin.description:
Up to 1.6.2 the NPC add-on and the VR build were separate downloads. They are both in this installer now.
If you still have them as separate mods, remove them before you install this. The VR patch matters most: it holds a DLL at the same path as this one, and depending on where it sits in your mod order it can put the old DLL back over the new one. Nothing in the installer can detect that for you, because the file has the same name either way.
Your boxes and settings are not in those mods and are not affected.

plugin.name: Skyrim Special Edition / Anniversary Edition
plugin.description: The normal build. Pick this unless you play in VR.

plugin.name: Skyrim VR
plugin.description:
Adds the VR notes. Nothing else changes.
Everything is identical across SE, AE and VR, the DLL included - it is one binary that works out which engine loaded it. Picking this only adds README_VR.txt, so if you install for SE and later move to VR you are not missing a file.
VR also needs SkyrimVRESL, and the SMF menu needs ImGui VR Helper. SkyUI VR on its own gives you the older MCM, which no longer reaches everything: NPC distribution, the Blocked list, the Recovery page, box renaming and any biped slot holding more than one box are SMF only.

plugin.name: NPC distribution
plugin.description:
Lets you publish a costume to NPCs and keep it on them across saves. Adds CostumeFW_NPC.esp and the carrier meshes the published and NPC-persist slots need.
Leave it off if you only dress your own character.

plugin.name: Enchantment passthrough (one full plugin, one light)
plugin.description:
Keeps a costume's enchantments, armor rating and tempering working while the costume is in a box. This is on by default in CEF's settings, and from 1.6.3 it needs CostumeFW_Abilities.esp. This option installs two files: that one and CostumeFW_Abilities2.esp.
CostumeFW_Abilities.esp is NOT light (ESL). It takes one of your 254 load-order slots, and it is the only CEF plugin that does - CostumeFW.esp, CostumeFW_BoxPool1.esp, CostumeFW_NPC.esp and CostumeFW_Abilities2.esp are all light and cost none.
It has to be a full plugin: the abilities live at fixed form IDs that your saves point at, and the flag cannot be changed later without changing how every one of them is addressed. That reasoning only applied to there being one pool, so the second one is light. Together they hold 3,072 abilities. A costume takes one the first time you capture it and another whenever its enchantment changes value, so heavy re-enchanting costs more than one; the Main page shows how many are left.
If you would rather not spend the slot, untick this. CEF will then turn enchantment passthrough off and say so, rather than falling back to the old method - the old method is what put stuck bonuses on people's characters, and quietly using it again would be worse than not doing it at all. Your costumes still look exactly the same; they just stop carrying stats.
Once you have used this, leave it installed. Your saves refer to those form IDs, and removing the plugin strands whatever was applied. That is also why this option is ticked and locked when CostumeFW_Abilities.esp is already active in your load order: at that point unticking it is not a choice, it is a way to lose the bonuses you have.
